title: Separating within-trial from across-trial component effect modification
question: Component ML-NMR fits one shared interaction on a globally centered covariate, which algebraically forces the causal within-trial interaction to equal the confounded across-trial association. How much does that cost, when, and is the damage really caused by aggregate data as the catalog claims?
design: Twelve-trial two-component Poisson network with a binary effect modifier whose prevalence varies across studies, aggregate arms generated by exact integration. 320 scenarios crossing network structure, the discordance between within-trial and across-trial modification, IPD availability including a case where one component has no within-trial data at all, arm size and prevalence spread. 2000 replicates each.
estimand: Within-trial component interaction on the conditional log-rate scale
answer: Fitting one shared interaction matrix on a globally centered covariate is not pooling: for a binary modifier with study prevalence p_s it is algebraically identical to imposing that the causal within-trial coefficient equals the confounded across-trial one. In the model simulated, coverage of a nominal 95% interval for the causal interaction falls from 93.8% when that happens to be true to 17.2% when the two are equal and opposite, and further in networks whose contrasts move two components at once. Separating them costs about 5% in interval width and removes an order of magnitude of bias. The catalog's stated cause is incomplete: the loss is present with all twelve trials supplying individual data, so aggregate data are not necessary for it, but removing individual data roughly doubles the bias, so they amplify it.
findings: Coverage under the shared restriction degrades monotonically with the discordance between the within-trial and across-trial coefficients, from 93.8% at no discordance to 17.2% when they are equal and opposite, and it is worse in bundled component networks whose contrasts move two components at once than where every contrast isolates one.
Both separated estimators are nominal at every discordance examined, 92.6% to 96.3%, including under a nonlinear across-trial pattern where the linear split model is itself misspecified.

CMP-13 says aggregate studies cause the pull. With all twelve trials supplying individual patient data the shared model still has median absolute standardized bias 0.15 and coverage as low as 44.6%, so aggregate data are not necessary. But bias rises to 0.29 and coverage falls to 17.2% as individual data are removed, so they amplify it. The registered refutation threshold was narrowly missed (47% of cells against 50%) and we report that rather than moving it.

Where a component appears in no individual-data arm, the three methods behave in three different ways: the IPD-anchored estimator declines to report it in 100% of replicates; the shared model returns a confident -0.34 against a truth of zero, sourced entirely from the across-trial gradient; and the joint split returns intervals so wide that coverage approaches one, when it returns one at all.

A study-clustered sandwich, included so the comparison could not be won on the variance estimator, covered 75.4% to 92.4% where the shared model is correctly specified. With twelve clusters it is badly anticonservative, and it is reported as a finding rather than used as the comparator.
not_answered: The registered global analysis is uninformative and the regime split that produced a usable answer was prompted by observing that failure, so it is not prespecified. The general headline about component ML-NMR is not established: the likelihood and nuisance structures are not mapped onto the fixed- and random-effect specifications the implemented method offers, and free study-by-treatment effects or priors can absorb or alter the term the identity isolates. A maximum-likelihood analogue of component ML-NMR. Implemented ML-NMR is Bayesian and priors matter most where interactions are weakly identified, so the coverage numbers do not transfer to multinma; the algebra does, and therefore so does the direction. One binary modifier, a log link, a Poisson outcome, additive components with no synergy, no random treatment-effect heterogeneity, no inconsistency, and exactly reported study prevalences. Under the discordance patterns the split model is correctly specified, so the study measures the cost of an algebraically known restriction rather than establishing that real networks contain within/across disagreement or how large it typically is. Continuous or multiple correlated modifiers, misspecified aggregate covariate distributions, and time-to-event outcomes are untested. It does not touch IDN-05.
peer_review: two rounds, two reviewers, both standing at major revision; the general headline is restricted to the specification simulated
